newsitem.title: USA: Gov. Pataki would defeat three NY Democrats - poll.
newsitem.headline: Gov. Pataki would defeat three NY Democrats - poll.

text.p: Republican Gov. George Pataki, 19 months away from running for a second term, would defeat any of the three top New York Democrats in the 1998 election, according to an opinion poll released Monday.
The poll by the Marist Institute for Public Opinion also found that New York voters were almost equally split in their approval of the way Pataki was doing his job.

In match-ups against possible Democratic Party candidates in the 1998 governor's race, Pataki would defeat former Gov. Mario Cuomo -- the man he beat in 1994 -- by the statistically tied margin of 46.4 percent to 45.8 percent with 7.8 percent undecided, according to Marist.

Pataki had an edge of 49.3 percent to 27.6 percent against U.S. Congressman Charles Schumer with 23 percent undecided, and 53.6 percent to 30.1 percent over New York State Comptroller Carl McCall with 16.3 percent undecided, according to the poll.
The survey of 603 registered voters was conducted by telephone March 17-19 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 4 percentage points, the institute said in a statement.
It revealed that 47 percent of the state's voters gave the governor a positive job approval rating while 49.9 percent regarded his performance after more than two years in office as "fair" or "poor."

A separate poll published this month by the Quinnipiac College of Hamden, Connecticut, found that Pataki, who won election on promises to cut taxes and restore the death penalty, had been boosted by a campaign for an environmental bond issue. His job rating in that poll was favourable by 56 to 34 percent.
